title: The story of Teddy Bears, by Letitia Snyman (U3A Overberg lecture)
summary: At the final U3A lecture of the year, Letitia Snyman presents ‘The Story of Teddy Bears’, on Friday 27 November at 10 am in the Catholic Church Hall.
description: Theodore (Teddy) Roosevelt was the 26th president of the United States, serving from 1901 to 1909. He was a very popular and effective president, often called the “first modern president” because of his extension of the power of the Executive during his two terms in office. He also involved himself and his country in international affairs and was the first American to win the Nobel Peace prize in 1905 for his role in negotiating an end to the war between Russia and Japan. In this presentation, we will also indulge in looking at another, more endearing and charming aspect of his legacy – the Teddy Bear! We invite you to share in the fun of looking at the origin and evolution of the phenomenon that is the stuffed animal toy that bears his name! Members are invited to bring Christmas presents for children in need, which the Hermanus Rotary Club will distribute.
profile: A morning lecture by the U3A Overberg, the University of the Third Age group in Hermanus, on the history of the teddy bear and its link to US president Theodore Roosevelt. Visitors sit in on a presentation in the Catholic Church Hall and pay a small door fee. It suits retired and older visitors with an interest in history.
